name: Benjamin
bio:
Benjamin is the youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, the last of Jacob's twelve sons, and Joseph's only full brother. Rachel died in difficult labor bearing him on the road to Bethlehem; with her dying breath she named him Ben-oni, "son of my sorrow," but his father Jacob renamed him Benjamin, "son of the right hand," replacing his mother's dying grief with a name of good fortune (Genesis 35:16-19).

Benjamin's birth was bound up with his mother's death, one of the most sorrowful moments in Jacob's family story — Jacob set up a pillar over her grave, showing how deeply he grieved the loss of his wife. Afterward, Benjamin became the son Jacob treasured most fiercely in his old age, hardly letting him out of his sight — when famine forced the other brothers to go to Egypt for grain, Jacob flatly refused to let Benjamin go with them, fearing some harm might befall him (Genesis 42:4, 38).

As Joseph's full brother, Benjamin plays a pivotal role at the climax of Joseph's story: when Joseph finally saw Benjamin again after years apart, he had him served five times as much food as the others, and secretly planted his own silver cup in Benjamin's sack to test whether his brothers had truly changed and were willing to take responsibility for their youngest brother — a test that led to Judah stepping forward, offering himself in Benjamin's place, and finally brought about Joseph's emotional reunion with his brothers (Genesis 43-45). Benjamin's story is an important witness to how Jacob's broken family moved from grief toward reconciliation and reunion.
